newsitem.title: USA: Mercury Finance adopts shareholder rights.
newsitem.headline: Mercury Finance adopts shareholder rights.

text.p: Mercury Finance Co said Thursday its board of directors unanimously approved a shareholder rights plan.

Mercury said it is not aware of any effort to acquire control of the company. The plan does not preclude the board from considering and accepting an offer it believes is in the best interest of the company, its creditors and shareholders, it added.

Mercury said the rights plan is designed to protect shareholders from what it called "abusive takeover tactics" and from attempts to acquire control of Mercury without offering a fair price to all of the company's shareholders.
Under the rights plan, a dividend distribution of one stock purchase right will be made for each share of common stock outstanding at the close of business on March 10, 1997.
Each right entitles the holder to purchase one share of Mercury common stock at a purchase price of $13.50. The plan has a 10-year duration.

The rights may become exercisable only if any person acquires beneficial ownership of 15 percent or more of Mercury common stock or begins a tender offer that could result in a 50 percent ownership, Mercury said.
All shareholders except for the acquiring person would then be entitled, by paying the right's exercise price, to buy Mercury common stock having twice the market value of the exercise price.

If there is a change in the majority of the board of directors before the rights become exercisable, the terms of the rights plan can be altered only by directors who were on the board before the change occurred. However, this limitation expires at six months after the change or one year from today, whichever is earlier.

Mercury said its board of directors can cancel the plan by redeeming the rights at a price of $0.001 a share in the event a proposed offer is considered to be in the best interest of Mercury, its creditors and shareholders.
